sections.text:
One cold winter night, Juha was invited to attend a luxurious dinner at the palace of one of the city's leading merchants and notables.

Juha had just returned from work in the field. His clothes were old, and his cloak was torn, with traces of dust and mud on it.

Due to his delay, Juha decided to go directly to the palace without passing through his house to change his clothes, believing that the merchant had invited him for his person and not his clothes.

When Juha arrived at the palace door, the guards looked at him with disgust and prevented him from entering, thinking that he was a beggar.

When Juha insisted that he was invited, they let him in, but the servants completely ignored him, and no one welcomed him. They sat him in the farthest place at the end of the hall, and offered him nothing but the remains of dry bread.

While the merchant welcomed the rich guests dressed in silk and brocade, seated them in the front of the council and offered them the most delicious meat and sweets.

Juha felt extremely insulted, so he quietly withdrew from the palace without anyone noticing him, and quickly ran home.

At home, Juha bathed and perfumed himself with the best perfumes, then put on his most beautiful clothes. A luxurious silk cloak, a new and decorated turban, and a large ring on his finger.

Then he returned again to the merchant's palace and stood proudly in front of the door.

As soon as the guards saw him in these luxurious clothes, they bowed to him respectfully and opened the doors wide for him.

The merchant who had invited him personally ran to receive him, took him by the hand, and seated him in the best place next to him at the front of the council.

He ordered the servants to serve the most delicious dishes of grilled meat and fried chicken in front of Juha personally.

Juha looked at the delicious food, then did something that shocked and amazed everyone!
Juha grabbed the edge of his wide silk abaya, and began to dip it in the broth and plates of meat, and said in an audible voice: “Eat, my clothes! Eat, my abaya! Here you go, eat of this delicious meat!”

The merchant was very surprised by this crazy behavior, and asked Juha, saying: “What are you doing, sensible Juha? Is it possible that you eat clothes?!”

Juha looked at the merchant with piercing eyes and a sarcastic smile and said: “Yes, sir, it is my clothes that should eat, not me!”

Juha added: “I came to you a while ago in my old, torn clothes, but you ignored me and sat me in the back and offered me nothing but dry bread.”

When I returned wearing my luxurious clothes, you received me warmly and served me the most delicious food!”

Then he raised his voice so that all the guests could hear: “So, the honor, respect, and food were not given to me (the human being, Juha), but rather to my silk clothes and my external appearance! It is fair for the clothes to eat what was given to them!”

The merchant hung his head in shame, and everyone realized the harsh lesson that Juha had taught them, that a person's true value lies in his essence and morals, and not in his appearance and the luxurious clothes that he wears.
